# search

> Search folders, projects, and users from a single endpoint.

Search folders, projects, and users from a single endpoint.

```graphql
search(
  query: String!
): [SearchResult!]!
```

### Arguments

#### [`search`.`query`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`String!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/string) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

Text matched against folder, project, and user names.

### Type

#### [`SearchResult`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/unions/search-result) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">union</badge>

A result returned from global workspace search.

### Example

```graphql
query SearchWorkspace($query: String!) {
  search(query: $query) {
    __typename
    ... on Folder {
      id
      name
    }
    ... on Project {
      id
      name
      status
    }
    ... on User {
      id
      name
      email
    }
  }
}
```

#### [`projectChanged`.`types`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`ProjectEventType!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/enums/project-event-type) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">list</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">enum</badge>

```graphql
    }
  }
```

The kind of change that occurred on a project.

# ProjectStatus

> The lifecycle stage of a project.

The lifecycle stage of a project.

```graphql
enum ProjectStatus {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
}
```

### Values

#### [`ProjectStatus`.`DRAFT`](#)

The project is being planned and is not yet active.

#### [`ProjectStatus`.`ACTIVE`](#)

The project is active and available to collaborators.

#### [`ProjectStatus`.`ARCHIVED`](#)

The project is retained for history and no longer active.

# Project

> A unit of work tracked in the workspace.

A unit of work tracked in the workspace.

```graphql
type Project implements Node {
  id: ID!
  name: String!
  status: ProjectStatus!
  owner: User!
  folder: Folder
  updatedAt: DateTime!
  state: String @deprecated
}
```

### Fields

#### [`Project`.`id`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`ID!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/id) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

The unique identifier of the project.

#### [`Project`.`name`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`String!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/string) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

The project name shown to collaborators.

#### [`Project`.`status`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`ProjectStatus!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/enums/project-status) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">enum</badge>

The current lifecycle stage of the project.

#### [`Project`.`owner`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`User!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/user) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

The user responsible for the project.

#### [`Project`.`folder`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`Folder`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/folder) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

The folder containing this project, when assigned.

#### [`Project`.`updatedAt`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`DateTime!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/date-time) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

When the project was last updated.

#### [`Project`.`state`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`String`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/string) <badge color="warning" size="sm" variant="subtle">deprecated</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

<accordion>
<accordion-item icon="i-lucide-archive" label="Deprecated">

Replaced by the `ProjectStatus` enum on status.

</accordion-item>
</accordion>

The project's lifecycle stage.

### Interfaces

#### [`Node`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/interfaces/node) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">interface</badge>

A globally unique entity identifier.

### Example

```graphql
  "id": "project_01",
  "name": "Mobile Refresh",
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "owner": {
    "id": "user_01",
    "name": "Avery Chen"
  },
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-05T10:15:00Z"
}
```

# ProjectConnection

> A paginated project result set.

A paginated project result set.

```graphql
type ProjectConnection {
  nodes: [Project!]!
  totalCount: Int!
}
```

### Fields

#### [`ProjectConnection`.`nodes`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`Project!!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/project) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

Projects in the current result page.

#### [`ProjectConnection`.`totalCount`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`Int!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/int) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

The total number of projects matching the query.

### Example

```graphql
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "project_01",
      "name": "Mobile Refresh",
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "owner": {
        "id": "user_01",
        "name": "Avery Chen"
      },
      "updatedAt": "2026-09-05T10:15:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Returned By

[`projects`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/operations/queries/projects)  <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">

query

</badge>


# ProjectEvent

> A change delivered to subscribers watching a project.

A change delivered to subscribers watching a project.

```graphql
type ProjectEvent {
  type: ProjectEventType!
  project: Project!
  actor: User
  occurredAt: DateTime!
}
```

### Fields

#### [`ProjectEvent`.`type`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`ProjectEventType!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/enums/project-event-type) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">enum</badge>

The kind of change that occurred.

#### [`ProjectEvent`.`project`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`Project!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/project) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

The project in its state after the change.

#### [`ProjectEvent`.`actor`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`User`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/user) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

The user who triggered the change, when known.

#### [`ProjectEvent`.`occurredAt`](#)<span className="gqlmd-mdx-bullet">●</span>[`DateTime!`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/scalars/date-time) <badge color="primary" size="sm" variant="subtle">non-null</badge> <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">scalar</badge>

When the change occurred.

### Example

```graphql
{
  "type": "UPDATED",
  "project": {
    "id": "project_01",
    "name": "Mobile Refresh",
    "status": "ACTIVE"
  },
  "occurredAt": "2026-09-05T10:15:00Z"
}
```

### Returned By

[`projectChanged`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/operations/subscriptions/project-changed)  <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">

subscription

</badge>

# ID

> The ID scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as "4") or integer (such as 4) input value will be accepted as an ID.

The `ID` scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as `"4"`) or integer (such as `4`) input value will be accepted as an ID.

```graphql
scalar ID
```

# SearchResult

> A result returned from global workspace search.

A result returned from global workspace search.

```graphql
union SearchResult = Folder | Project | User
```

### Possible types

#### [`SearchResult`.`Folder`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/folder) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

A virtual folder used to organize workspace resources.

#### [`SearchResult`.`Project`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/project) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

A unit of work tracked in the workspace.

#### [`SearchResult`.`User`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/types/objects/user) <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">object</badge>

A workspace member who owns and collaborates on projects.

### Returned By

[`search`](https://graphql-markdown.dev/docs/operations/queries/search)  <badge color="neutral" size="sm" variant="subtle">

query

</badge>
